- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, true price often lags and reverses — adjust downward by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.  
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model overfits recent highs/lows; apply smoothing filter or use 3-period moving average for correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in high-sentiment environments; apply sentiment-weighted decay: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per 1 unit of sentiment above 0.5.  
- If true price drops sharply after model peak, sentiment often turns negative — anticipate further decline; add 1–2% buffer below forecast for next 5 days.
